DEVELOPMENT OF A NEW TRADE MODELING FRAMEWORK TO ALLOW FOR MORE PRECISE, DISAGGREGATED IMPACT RESULTS - RANGELAND ECOSYSTEM DYSFUNCTION ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED WILDFIRE ACTIVITY, INVASIVE ANNUAL GRASSES, AND EXPANDING CONIFERS IS NEGATIVELY IMPACTING AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AND A VARIETY OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES ACROSS THE WESTERN UNITED STATES. THESE FACTORS HAVE SEVERE ECONOMIC IMPLICATIONS; FOR EXAMPLE, FEDERAL FIRE SUPPRESSION EXPENDITURES IN FY 2017 APPROACHED $3 BILLION. THE INCREASING FREQUENCY OF WILDFIRES ACROSS WESTERN RANGELANDS REMAINS A THREAT TO ECOSYSTEM STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION. IN GREAT BASIN RANGELANDS, WILDFIRE OFTEN CREATES A POSITIVE FEEDBACK BY INCREASING INVASIVE ANNUALS AND ALTERING FUEL LOADING. UNDERSTANDING THE DYNAMICS OF THE PLANT COMMUNITY-BOTH IN RESPONSE TO WILDFIRE AND ITS ROLE IN WILDFIRE OCCURRENCE-IS CRITICAL TO GUIDE RANGELAND MANAGEMENT IN THE FACE OF FIRE, FUELS, AND INVASIVE PLANTS. AT LARGE SPATIAL SCALES, EXISTING FUEL MODELING EFFORTS HAVE SHOWN THAT ANTECEDENT PRECIPITATION AMOUNT AND PATTERN CAN BE USED TO GENERALIZE WILDFIRE PROBABILITY. MISSING FROM THOSE EFFORTS HAS BEEN THE INCORPORATION OF BIOTIC STATUS (E.G., PLANT COMMUNITY COMPOSITION AND FUNCTIONAL GROUP ABUNDANCE) INTO PREDICTIVE MODELS. INCORPORATING CURRENT BIOTIC INFORMATION HAS THE POTENTIAL TO DRAMATICALLY IMPROVE THE RELEVANCY OF EMPIRICALLY-DERIVED MODELS TO ON-THE-GROUND MANAGEMENT CONDITIONS AND DECISION MAKING. THE OBJECTIVES OF THIS WORK ARE TO 1) EXAMINE THE BIOTIC DRIVERS OF AND RESPONSES TO WILDFIRE; AND 2) EXAMINE THE POTENTIAL FOR INCORPORATING BIOTIC COMPONENTS INTO ABIOTICALLY-DRIVEN (E.G., PRECIPITATION AT VARIOUS TIME LAGS) MODELS FOR PREDICTING WILDFIRE AND PLANT COMMUNITY RESPONSES. OBJECTIVES WILL APPLY ACROSS THE GREAT BASIN REGION.

FEDERAL NUTRITION ASSISTANCE, FOOD INSUFFICIENCY, AND HEALTH AND HEALTH CARE OUTCOMES AMONG HOUSEHOLDS WITH AND WITHOUT CHILDREN WITH SPECIA - OBTAIN AND ANALYZE GENE EXPRESSION DATA USING RNA SEQUENCING ON A SERIES OF OAT LINES THAT HAVE BEEN CHARACTERIZED FOR NUTRITIONAL QUALITY AND HAVE BEEN ASSAYED USING HIGH-THROUGHPUT METABOLOMICS OF MATURE GRAIN. THESE LINES HAVE ALSO BEEN GENOTYPED BY SEQUENCING REDUCED REPRESENTATIONS OF THEIR GENOMES. DIFFERENTIAL GENE EXPRESSION AND CORRELATION BETWEEN GENE EXPRESSION, METABOLOMICS PROFILES, AND NUTRITIONAL QUALITY WILL BE USED TO IDENTIFY LOCI HARBORING GENETIC VARIATION THAT AFFECTS NUTRITIONAL QUALITY. THESE DATA WILL ALSO ENABLE PREDICTION OF NUTRITIONAL QUALITY FOR NEWLY DEVELOPED OAT LINES.

UNDERSTANDING SNAP AND FOOD SECURITY AMONG LOW-INCOME HOUSEHOLDS - INFECTIONS WITH HERPES VIRUSES ARE KNOWN TO GENERATE POWERFUL CD8 T CELL RESPONSES AND THERE IS A LARGE BODY OF EVIDENCE INDICATING THAT THESE RESPONSES PLAY A KEY ROLE IN IMMUNITY TO THESE VIRUSES. THIS HAS PROMPTED RESEARCH TO EXPLORE THE POTENTIAL OF CERTAIN HERPES VIRUSES AS VACCINE VECTORS, FOCUSING PARTICULARLY ON DISEASES THAT REQUIRE CD8 T CELL RESPONSES FOR IMMUNITY. THE CAPACITY OF CD8 T CELLS TO ACT AS EFFECTORS AGAINST VIRAL INFECTIONS GENERALLY RELIES ON THEIR ABILITY TO RECOGNISE AND RESPOND TO VIRUS-INFECTED CELLS BEFORE THEY PRODUCE LARGE QUANTITIES OF VIRUS. IN THIS REGARD, CD8 T CELL RESPONSES TO HERPES VIRUSES SUCH AS HUMAN HERPES SIMPLEX VIRUS (HSV-1) TEND TO INCLUDE DOMINANT RESPONSES AGAINST THE IE PROTEINS AND IT IS THESE RESPONSES THAT ARE PREDOMINANTLY INVOLVED IN MEDIATING IMMUNE PROTECTION. IN ADDITION, A NUMBER OF HERPES VIRUSES HAVE A PREFERENTIAL TROPISM FOR MACROPHAGES AND DENDRITIC CELLS, THUS ENABLING THE INFECTED CELLS THEMSELVES TO ACT AS ANTIGEN-PRESENTING CELLS FOR INDUCTION OF CD8 T CELL RESPONSES. ONE SUCH GROUP IS THE CYTOMEGALOVIRUSES (CMV), WHICH IN HUMANS CAUSE ASYMPTOMATIC INFECTIONS IN HEALTHY PEOPLE BUT CAN BE PATHOGENIC IN IMMUNOCOMPROMISED INDIVIDUALS. MOREOVER, SINCE CMVS ARE POOR INDUCERS OF NEUTRALISING ANTIBODIES, A CD8 T CELL RESPONSE CAN STILL BE INDUCED FOLLOWING IMMUNIZATION OF PREVIOUSLY INFECTED INDIVIDUALS. THE COMBINATION OF THESE PROPERTIES MAKES CMVS AN ATTRACTIVE PROSPECT FOR USE AS VACCINE VECTORS. RECENT STUDIES UTILISING SIMIAN CMV AS A VECTOR FOR DELIVERY OF SIMIAN IMMUNODEFICIENCY VIRAL ANTIGENS HAVE SHOWN THAT IT INDUCES STRONG VIRUS-SPECIFIC CD8 T CELL RESPONSES AND HIGH LEVELS OF PROTECTION AGAINST VIRUS CHALLENGE. ALTHOUGH A CYTOMEGALOVIRUS HAS NOT BEEN IDENTIFIED IN CATTLE, BOVINE HERPES VIRUS 4 (BHV-4) SHARES A NUMBER OF PROPERTIES WITH CYTOMEGALOVIRUSES, WHICH HIGHLIGHT ITS POTENTIAL AS A VECTOR. ORIGINALLY CLASSIFIED AS A B-HERPES VIRUS AND REFERRED TO AS BOVINE CYTOMEGALOVIRUS, BASED ON ITS BIOLOGICAL PROPERTIES, BHV-4 WAS SUBSEQUENTLY FOUND TO BE A '-HERPES VIRUS. INFECTION WITH BHV-4 IS PREVALENT IN EUROPE AND USA AND ALTHOUGH THE VIRUS HAS BEEN ISOLATED FREQUENTLY FROM BOTH NORMAL AND DISEASED BOVINE TISSUES, THERE IS CURRENTLY NO EVIDENCE THAT IT IS THE CAUSATIVE AGENT OF DISEASE. LIKE CYTOMEGALOVIRUSES, BHV-4 IS REPORTED TO HAVE A PREDILECTION FOR THE MACROPHAGE LINEAGE AND IT INDUCES POOR NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODY RESPONSES. HENCE, IT IS LIKELY TO GENERATE CELLULAR IMMUNE RESPONSES IN PREVIOUSLY INFECTED ANIMALS AND COULD POTENTIALLY BE ADMINISTERED ON MORE THAN ONE OCCASION TO BOOST CELLULAR IMMUNE RESPONSES. BHV-4 HAS BEEN DEVELOPED AS A VACCINE VECTOR BY DR. GAITANO DONOFRIA, WHO HAS PRODUCED SEVERAL RECOMBINANT BHV-4 VIRUSES EXPRESSING VIRAL PROTEINS AND SHOWN THAT THEY STIMULATE STRONG ANTIBODY RESPONSES IN CALVES AND PROTECTION AGAINST THE RESPECTIVE VIRUSES. HOWEVER, THE ABILITY OF THE VIRUS TO INDUCE CELLULAR IMMUNE RESPONSES HAS NOT BEEN INVESTIGATED.

DEVELOPMENT OF A NEW TRADE MODELING FRAMEWORK TO ALLOW FOR MORE PRECISE, DISAGGREGATED IMPACT RESULTS - RANGELAND ECOSYSTEM DYSFUNCTION ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED WILDFIRE ACTIVITY, INVASIVE ANNUAL GRASSES, AND EXPANDING CONIFERS IS NEGATIVELY IMPACTING AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AND A VARIETY OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES ACROSS THE WESTERN UNITED STATES. THESE FACTORS HAVE SEVERE ECONOMIC IMPLICATIONS; FOR EXAMPLE, FEDERAL FIRE SUPPRESSION EXPENDITURES IN FY 2017 APPROACHED $3 BILLION. THE INCREASING FREQUENCY OF WILDFIRES ACROSS WESTERN RANGELANDS REMAINS A THREAT TO ECOSYSTEM STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION. IN GREAT BASIN RANGELANDS, WILDFIRE OFTEN CREATES A POSITIVE FEEDBACK BY INCREASING INVASIVE ANNUALS AND ALTERING FUEL LOADING. UNDERSTANDING THE DYNAMICS OF THE PLANT COMMUNITY-BOTH IN RESPONSE TO WILDFIRE AND ITS ROLE IN WILDFIRE OCCURRENCE-IS CRITICAL TO GUIDE RANGELAND MANAGEMENT IN THE FACE OF FIRE, FUELS, AND INVASIVE PLANTS. AT LARGE SPATIAL SCALES, EXISTING FUEL MODELING EFFORTS HAVE SHOWN THAT ANTECEDENT PRECIPITATION AMOUNT AND PATTERN CAN BE USED TO GENERALIZE WILDFIRE PROBABILITY. MISSING FROM THOSE EFFORTS HAS BEEN THE INCORPORATION OF BIOTIC STATUS (E.G., PLANT COMMUNITY COMPOSITION AND FUNCTIONAL GROUP ABUNDANCE) INTO PREDICTIVE MODELS. INCORPORATING CURRENT BIOTIC INFORMATION HAS THE POTENTIAL TO DRAMATICALLY IMPROVE THE RELEVANCY OF EMPIRICALLY-DERIVED MODELS TO ON-THE-GROUND MANAGEMENT CONDITIONS AND DECISION MAKING. THE OBJECTIVES OF THIS WORK ARE TO 1) EXAMINE THE BIOTIC DRIVERS OF AND RESPONSES TO WILDFIRE; AND 2) EXAMINE THE POTENTIAL FOR INCORPORATING BIOTIC COMPONENTS INTO ABIOTICALLY-DRIVEN (E.G., PRECIPITATION AT VARIOUS TIME LAGS) MODELS FOR PREDICTING WILDFIRE AND PLANT COMMUNITY RESPONSES. OBJECTIVES WILL APPLY ACROSS THE GREAT BASIN REGION.
